topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Visual Language of Motion
target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: Pixel the Cat and the Grid
lecture_lines: Welcome to the coordinate plane, our mathematical playground.
Meet Pixel, our character positioned at the grid center.
A vector arrow locates his nose precisely in space.
Multiple vectors together define his entire visual shape.
Transforming means moving every point in a systematic way.
animations: Fade in a coordinate grid (#888888) with Pixel the Cat (a simple shape) at the center.
Draw a white vector (#FFFFFF) to Pixel's nose and several light blue vectors (#ADD8E6) to his features.
Animate the entire grid and Pixel shifting together to a new position.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Meet the basis vectors, i-hat and j-hat, our building blocks.
Scale these arrows to reach any point in space.
We label these unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
animations: Show a coordinate grid (#444444) and a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (3, 2) to represent a generic point.
Animate a red arrow (#FF0000) from (0,0) to (1,0) labeled 'i-hat' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate a green arrow (#00FF00) from (0,0) to (0,1) labeled 'j-hat' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show the red arrow scaling to length 3 and green arrow scaling to length 2, summing to reach the point (3, 2).
Highlight the original i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) vectors with a yellow flash (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Rules of Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: A transformation is linear if the origin stays fixed.
Grid lines must remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced.
This ensures space stretches without warping into curves.
animations: Show a grid. Keep the origin point (0,0) as a large white dot (#FFFFFF).
Animate the grid lines tilting while remaining straight, parallel, and evenly spaced.
Briefly show the grid lines curving wildly, then snap them back to being straight with a green flash (#90EE90).

sections.title: Encoding Motion into a Matrix
lecture_lines: We start with the standard basis vectors on the grid.
Watch as i-hat and j-hat move to new locations.
A 2x2 matrix records these final basis positions.
The first column captures the coordinates of transformed i-hat.
The second column captures the coordinates of transformed j-hat.
animations: Display the standard i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) unit vectors on a static grid.
Animate i-hat moving to (2, 1) and j-hat moving to (-1, 1) as the grid transforms.
Show a pair of empty matrix brackets [ ] appearing on the right side of the screen.
Animate the coordinates of the new i-hat (2, 1) moving into the first column of the matrix (#FF0000).
Animate the coordinates of the new j-hat (-1, 1) moving into the second column of the matrix (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Calculation: Transforming Pixel
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication is a recipe for transforming any point.
Highlight the first column and the original x-coordinate.
Scale the new i-hat by his original x-coordinate.
Add the new j-hat scaled by his original y-coordinate.
His nose lands precisely at its new calculated location.
animations: Display the 2x2 matrix and Pixel's nose vector [1, 1] side-by-side as a calculation.
Highlight the first column of the matrix and the nose's original x-coordinate (1).
Show the transformed i-hat vector [2, 1] being scaled by the nose's x-coordinate.
Scale the transformed j-hat [-1, 1] by the nose's y-coordinate (1) and visually sum the vectors.
Move the blue nose dot (#0000FF) to the resulting position [1, 2] on the transformed grid.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Matrices describe how we manipulate space and shapes.
This math powers video game graphics and photo filters.
Linear transformations bring the digital world to life.
animations: Show Pixel the Cat rotating 45 degrees. Display a rotation matrix in yellow (#FFFF00).
Show Pixel stretching horizontally. Display a scaling matrix in yellow (#FFFF00).
Fade out everything and display 'Linear Transformations' in center with gold color (#FFD700).
